answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it earns reputation, then randomly assign staked peers to audit one another’s signed work. If audits find fabricated identities or copied evidence, the protocol burns the offender’s stake and lowers its weight; honest auditors share a reward. A quartz beacon may publish the random audit seed, while zephyr names a sample task. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many accounts and risk losing each stake, rather than gaining influence by creating identities alone.
